segments.text: In accordance with regulations, I request Your Excellency, after consulting the Board, to request from the Minister of State for Defense information about the identification, location, and concise content of all documentation containing evidentiary, operational, functional, or personal information, generated by military or civilian personnel, under the custody of the Brazilian Army, originating and classified between the years 1996 and 1997, and in subsequent years if correlatable. Specifically, I request the information regarding generation and collection under the orders of the Military Command of the East and in the lower instances of the 43rd RM/4 3 DE, from which the Military Sergeant School of Arms (ESA) is subordinate.

I also request any information that may have originated from orders issued by higher authorities, up to the Army Command in Brasília, if they refer to any extraordinary occurrence or operation recorded in that OM during the mentioned years. That this list of documents, to be sent to this deputy,
includes all classified information according to the legislation in force at the time, those re-classified and
those with secrecy periods extended from these years cited to the entry into force of
the current Law of Access to Information (LAI - Law 12.527/2011), or access reservation,
as per this same LAI, subsequent decrees, ordinances, and instructions. I further request
that such data be provided, as per the examples in the attached tables (I and II).
JUSTIFICATION

It is the responsibility of this federal deputy to present two Information Requests from the Chamber of Deputies regarding this issue, namely, the access of the Brazilian citizen to classified information related to the registration and study of unidentified flying objects (UFOs) and their crew, a field known as ufology: RICs 44 70/2009 and 679/2011. Both answered in parts by the three Armed Forces, in representation of the Ministry of Defense to a greater extent, and within what the Forces affirm to be the reported truth.

in files of their subordinate agencies, they confirmed not only the existence of such information, but also some incidents involving alleged UFOs and their crew, as well as the seriousness with which at least the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) handles the subject. We have, today, over 10,000 pages of documents and other types of
information in various formats, in batches collected and in possession of the National Archive,
in Brasília and Rio de Janeiro, entirely sent by FAB. That without counting the
procedural norms of this Force, regarding the process of collection, registration and
archiving, with the subsequent collection of the material to public archives. Such
procedures are outlined in the Portaria 551/GC3 of August 9, 2010, published by the
FAB and known among scholars of the subject and in specific media as the "OVNI
Act." However, despite the efforts demonstrated by the Brazilian Air Force, many issues raised in previous requests remain pending. Over time, seven years have passed since the responses to the last RIC-, and there is no longer the same willingness from the other branches, the Army and Navy, to provide data to interested citizens, as the same phenomenon that led FAB to adopt and publish its procedures for recording and filing occurs not only in the air space but also over and under Brazilian territorial waters, and its activities are also recorded on land, in the over 8.5 million square kilometers of Brazilian territory, making it a matter to be addressed not by one but by all three branches of the national defense forces. In particular, the justification for this Request is based on the pursuit of information regarding a specific case of significant national impact and global resonance, known in the media as "The Varginha ET Case" or among ufologists as "The Varginha Case," due to its occurrence in that Minas Gerais city in early 1996 and its press coverage that lasted for at least another year. This case is of unparalleled importance for several reasons, but two are of paramount importance to scientific knowledge and the transparency of public acts. First, because, according to UFOlogists, it involves the crash of an unknown-technology UFO and the capture of at least two of its crew, and second, due to the impressive cover-up operation of the facts, for reasons that are still not very clear. Suspicions also lead to another serious conclusion, due to a possible breach of national sovereignty, embodied in the final destination of the wreckage of the crashed ship and the seized bodies, which, according to ufologists, according to the military involved, were taken to the United States of America against the wishes of several officers, for obvious reasons. The lack of public information about the case, considered genuine by a large part of the population of Varginha, results in prejudice, ridicule, embarrassment, pain, and doubt among witnesses and relatives of those directly involved, such as the family of military police officer Marco Eli Chereze, who is said to have been a fatal victim of direct contact with one of the crew members. Under the LAI, which was sanctioned after the aforementioned RICs were answered, new questions about the procedure, especially from the Army, were raised. Since 2012, numerous requests have been made to the Electronic System of the Citizen Information Service (e-SIC) of the Federal Government, all of which have been denied or handled in a way that does not reveal what may remain classified. It's the case, for example,

from the strange absence, to this moment, on the Army's website, of the Indexing Codes of Documents Containing Secret Information (CIDICs) originating in the years 1996 and 1997. Article 45, Item 11 of Decree No. 7,724, one of the decrees that emerged to complement and give effect to LAI (Law on Access to Information), stipulates that all still classified documents have their identifications made available in a specific list, on the electronic pages of the public bodies responsible for them, by June 1st of each year. If these documents do indeed exist and were generated between 1996 and 1997, as numerous circumstantial and testimonial evidence show;
to remain classified, they must have been categorized at the time as ULTRASECRET, with a 25-year secrecy period. By the way, one of the main military witnesses in the Varginha Case categorically stated in a recorded deposition that the 'transfer of unknown biological entities, crew members of the crashed UFO, implemented on January 23, 1996 from ESA to Campinas (Unicamp), was treated as ultra-secret by the commanders, thus classified in that category. Thus, their records could only be made available for public consultation on January 24, 2021, although the CIDIC that identifies it should already exist and be available to those interested. Now, if Decree 7,724 entered into force on May 16, 2012, why has the Army not yet made available in its "list of ultra-secret information" the CIDICs (or incident reports) for this and other occurrences in the Varginha Case, six years after the LAI (Law on Access to Information) came into effect?

In this guide
prepared by CGU, in its subitem B.2.4. - The content of the "classified information" area reads clearly: "It is also recommended that the agency or entity disclose the subject matter of the classified document, with the aim of increasing transparency regarding its content, as well as allowing social control. Note that the inclusion of the subject in the list of classified documents assists in identifying future references, as provided for in Article 30, item 11, of Law No. 12.527/2011. For that, the
agency must inform the content of the document in the most comprehensive way possible, without, however,
disclosing the nature of the restricted information. This recommendation is simply ignored by the Army.

It also draws attention to this list of classified documents marked as "ultra-secret," where only those whose secrecy periods expire or in the previous year, or in the year of the list's publication, up to June 1st, are made public. Thus, as of June 1st, 2017 - the last update was made in 2016 - all ultra-secret documents were nearing the end of their secrecy periods, meaning those originating up to 1992, twenty-five years prior. None in this category have been classified as ultra-secret after 1992. It's also notable that all documents classified in this category already have approved reclassification suggestions, meaning an additional twenty-five years of secrecy. There is no record of a document classified at the highest level of secrecy that has not been reclassified, let alone one that has.

Response:
Article 30 of the LAI (Law on National Security Information) stipulates that lists of classified and declassified information be published annually on a website, as follows:

"Article 30. [...]" The highest authority of each public body or entity shall, annually, publish on a website dedicated to the dissemination of administrative data and information, in accordance with regulations:

I. A list of information that has been declassified in the last 12 (twelve) months;

/1. A list of classified documents in each level of secrecy, with identification for future reference;

f. A statistical report containing the number of information requests received, fulfilled, and denied, as well as generic information about the requesters.

§I. Public bodies and entities shall maintain a copy of the publication mentioned in the preceding paragraph for public consultation at their headquarters.

§r. Public bodies and entities shall maintain an extract with a list of classified information, accompanied by the date, level of secrecy, and grounds for classification. "

The publication of rolls by the Brazilian Army follows the prescribed legislation, in accordance with the aforementioned article. Regarding the recommendation in the guide, the identification of documents is done by CIDIC, which is unique to each document. Thus, it is verified that the legal obligation resulting from the LAI (Law of Access to Information) is fully met through the annual publication of rolls.

IV - "It also draws attention to this list of classified documents as ultra-secret, where only those whose secrecy periods expire or in the previous year, or in the year of roll publication, up to June 30th, are published. Thus, as of June 2017 (the last update was done in 2016), all ultra-secret documents were about to lose their secrecy period, that is, those that had their origin recorded up to 1992, twenty-five years prior. There is none in this category classified as ultra-secret after 1992. It is also noted that all those classified in this category already have the approved suggestion for reclassification, that is, with an additional twenty-five years of secrecy. There is no record of a document classified at the highest level of secrecy that has not been reclassified, nor has it been declassified after the LAI came into effect. If this logic, which prioritizes the exception over the rule for maintaining secrecy, persists rather than the LAI's recommendation of transparency, the first documents on the Varginha Case will only have their CIDICs disclosed at the expiration of their secrecy period in 2021, and already reclassified in the same category, remaining hidden from society until 2046.

              Response:
            Classified documents at the ultra-secret level are listed in the classified
documents registers. The first register was published in 2014, covering the years of
2013/2014, as prescribed by the General Instructions for the Assessment and Control of
Classified Documents - (EB10-IG-01.015), and published after the entry into force of the AI.

Classified documents at the ultra-secret level are subject to extension of classification
for up to 25 (twenty-five) years by the Joint Commission for the Reassessment of Information
(CMRI), in accordance with Article 35, paragraph 1, item (i) of the AI:

"Article 35 (VETTED)
§ 1. The Joint Commission for the Reassessment of Information is established to decide,
within the scope of the Federal Public Administration, on the treatment and classification of
secret information, and shall be competent to:
I. Request from the authority that classified information as ultra-secret or secret
clarification or content, partial or full, of the information;
II. Review the classification of ultra-secret or secret information, either ex officio or
at the request of an interested party, in accordance with the provisions of Article r and other
provisions of this Law; and
III. Extend the secrecy period of ultra-secretly classified information, always for a
determined period, while its access or disclosure may pose an external threat to national
sovereignty or the integrity of national territory or a serious risk to the country's
international relations, observing the period provided for in Article 24, paragraph 1."

The Brazilian Army's ultra-secret documents had their classification extended by the
CMRI through the decision on the ex-officio review of classified information n°
001/2016-CMRI, dated 23 AGO 16, and the decision on the extension of classified
information n° 002/2016-CMRI, also on 23 AGO 16, and were included in the register
of classified documents at the ultra-secret level for the years of 2015/2016,
available on the Brazilian Army's classified/declassified information website under the
item "Ultra-Secret Information Register 2015/2016" updated.

3. From the analyses conducted on a reported occurrence of the fall of an Unidentified

documents or information on the subject in the Brazilian Army, except for the one sent via
Ofício n° 9228-GM/ASPAR-MD, dated 16 August 2011, to this Legislative House in response to
Information Request n° 679, 2011, from the same author of this Information Request.

4. Finally, I am available for any additional clarifications that Your Excellency may
consider necessary.
